nodes.summary: An annotated command is built like an IMP command, from skip, assignments $x := a$ of an arithmetic expression $a$ to a variable $x$ (a natural number), sequential composition $C_1;\,C_2$ and conditionals $\mathrm{if}\ b\ \mathrm{then}\ C_1\ \mathrm{else}\ C_2$ on a boolean expression $b$, except that every while loop $\{I\}\ \mathrm{while}\ b\ \mathrm{do}\ C$ also carries an assertion $I$, its invariant.
nodes.title: Annotated commands

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an annotated command and $Q$, $Q'$ assertions such that $Q$ entails $Q'$, and write $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ for the precondition and the verification condition of $C$ for the postcondition $Q$. If $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, then $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ entails $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q')$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q')$ holds.
nodes.title: Weakening the postcondition of an annotated command

nodes.summary: For an annotated command $C$ and an assertion $Q$ (the postcondition), the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ is the assertion computed backwards as follows: $\mathrm{pre}(\mathrm{skip}, Q) = Q$; $\mathrm{pre}(x := a, Q)$ holds in a state $s$ iff $Q$ holds in the state obtained from $s$ by giving $x$ the value of $a$ in $s$; $\mathrm{pre}(C_1;\,C_2, Q) = \mathrm{pre}(C_1, \mathrm{pre}(C_2, Q))$; the precondition of…
nodes.title: Precondition of an annotated command

nodes.summary: The IMP command $\mathrm{strip}(C)$ underlying an annotated command $C$ is obtained by deleting the invariant of every while loop: skip, assignments, sequential composition and conditionals are kept with their parts stripped, and $\{I\}\ \mathrm{while}\ b\ \mathrm{do}\ C'$ becomes $\mathrm{while}\ b\ \mathrm{do}\ \mathrm{strip}(C')$.
nodes.title: Erasing annotations

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be an IMP command and $P$, $Q$ assertions such that the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\ c\ \{Q\}$ is valid. Then there is an annotated command $C$ such that erasing its loop invariants gives $c$, that is $\mathrm{strip}(C) = c$, the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, and $P$ entails the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$.
nodes.title: Completeness of verification conditions for valid triples

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be an IMP command and $P$, $Q$ assertions such that the Hoare triple $\{P\}\ c\ \{Q\}$ is derivable in the partial-correctness Hoare logic. Then there is an annotated command $C$ such that erasing its loop invariants gives $c$, that is $\mathrm{strip}(C) = c$, the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, and $P$ entails the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$.
nodes.title: Completeness of verification conditions for derivable triples

nodes.summary: For an annotated command $C$ and an assertion $Q$, write $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ for the precondition and the verification condition of $C$ for the postcondition $Q$, and $\mathrm{strip}(C)$ for the IMP command obtained from $C$ by erasing its loop invariants. For every such $C$ and $Q$, if $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, then the Hoare triple $\{\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)\}\ \mathrm{strip}(C)\ \{Q\}$ is…
nodes.title: Soundness of verification conditions

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an annotated command, let $\mathrm{strip}(C)$ be the IMP command obtained from $C$ by erasing its loop invariants, and let $P$, $Q$ be assertions. If the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds and $P$ entails the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$, then the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\ \mathrm{strip}(C)\ \{Q\}$ is valid.
nodes.title: Verification conditions yield valid Hoare triples

nodes.summary: For an annotated command $C$ and an assertion $Q$ (the postcondition), the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ is the proposition defined as follows, where $\mathrm{pre}$ is the precondition of an annotated command: $\mathrm{vc}(\mathrm{skip}, Q)$ and $\mathrm{vc}(x := a, Q)$ are true; $\mathrm{vc}(C_1;\,C_2, Q)$ holds iff $\mathrm{vc}(C_1, \mathrm{pre}(C_2, Q))$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C_2, Q)$ hold; the…
nodes.title: Verification condition of an annotated command

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
